how_to_read: sentences[].w = first..last word id inside this chapter; word k (0-based) of the sentence is first+k and `ar` is the spoken text (its space-separated tokens are those words); fr = [start_frame, end_frame] at 24 fps from the word map; impact = hook words (id=text); num = spoken numbers with data-contract fact ids; first_mention = glossary terms to chip (id=term); dup = same claim in another chapter. Anchor with {word, lead_frames} only. Visual candidates are ideas, never footage.

constraints.anchors: {word, lead_frames} only; never seconds or frames; event frame = word start - lead_frames
constraints.lead_frames: kinetic word -3, graphic state change -2, shot cut -4..-6 (inside a pause >= 200 ms), counter starts at the number word
constraints.density: >= 20 events/min; no gap > 4 s without an event (hold <= 6 s with reason); shot median 6-12 s, max 25 s (shots > 12 s: an event every 3 s)
constraints.coverage: every sentence >= 1 anchored event; >= 80 % of sentences a mechanism event; every spoken number and every first-mention term on screen
constraints.kinetic: 8-20 kinetic words per minute; <= 6 words and <= 2 lines on screen; impact word 1-2 words
constraints.fx: hero (real-time 3D) <= 5 % of chapter frames (ADR-002 RT5); fx_tier lite|standard|hero
constraints.text: text on busy backgrounds needs a plate or halo; sizes and safe areas: 04 sections 3.2 and 3.4
banned: invented numbers (every number: data-contract id or source sentence)
constraints.components: use only frozen components (harness/schemas/components/); requests go to corpus/specs/_component_requests.jsonl
constraints.chapter_rhythm: problem -> mental model -> progressive visual -> worked example -> prediction -> failure (crit) -> fix (ok) -> callback -> artifact (per chapter, not per sentence)

sentences.ar: الكمبيوتر بيعمل حاجة واحدة، بسرعة رهيبة، ومكررة: بيجيب instruction، بيفكّها، وينفّذها.
sentences.en: A computer does one thing, extremely fast, over and over: it fetches an instruction, decodes it, and executes it.

sentences.ar: بصّ على المؤشر وهو ماشي دي الماكينة كلها.
sentences.en: Watch the pointer move — that is the whole machine.

sentences.ar: والداتا بتعيش في مكانين، والفرق بينهم هو اللي هيحدد أغلب مشاكل الأداء اللي هتقابلك بعدين.
sentences.en: Data lives in two places and the difference decides most of your future performance problems.

sentences.ar: الـRAM سريعة وليها عناوين، وبتنسى كل حاجة أول ما البرنامج يقف.
sentences.en: RAM is fast, addressed, and forgets everything the moment the program stops.

sentences.ar: القراءة من الميموري بالـnanoseconds؛ القراءة من الديسك بالـmicroseconds أو الـmilliseconds
sentences.en: Reading from memory takes nanoseconds; reading from disk takes microseconds or milliseconds.

sentences.ar: والفرق ده هو السبب إن الـdatabase بتعمل index، وإن Spark بيعمل cache،
sentences.en: That gap is why a database keeps an index, why Spark caches,

sentences.ar: وإن برنامجك بيقع على ملف كبير وشغال تمام على ملف صغير.
sentences.en: and why your program dies on a big file but works on a small one.

sentences.ar: دلوقتي أصغر وحدة. الـbyte عبارة عن تمن مفاتيح، يعني بيشيل 256 قيمة مختلفة.
sentences.en: Now, the smallest unit: a byte is eight switches, so it holds 256 different values.
A number is a byte pattern.

sentences.ar: والحرف كمان نمط bytes بس بس لأننا كلنا اتفقنا أي نمط يعني أي حرف.
sentences.en: A letter is also a byte pattern — but only because we all agreed on which pattern means which letter.
That agreement is called an encoding.

sentences.ar: في UTF-8، الكلمة دي من أربع حروف وطولها خمس bytes، لأن الحرف اللي عليه علامة محتاج اتنين.
sentences.en: In UTF-8, this four-letter word is five bytes long, because the accented character needs two.

sentences.ar: وكل UnicodeDecodeError غامضة هتقابلك في حياتك هي الجملة دي وهي بتقع عليك على شكل crash.
sentences.en: Every mysterious UnicodeDecodeError you will ever meet is that sentence, arriving as a crash.

facts.rule: A number goes on screen with its fact id as `ref`/`data_refs`. `unmatched_numbers` are spoken but have no data-contract fact: their source is the sentence itself (a valid `s:` ref); never replace them with a different figure.

glossary.rule: Explain the term in Egyptian Arabic the first time it appears; then use the original term naturally, in Latin script, inside Arabic sentences.
glossary.register_ar: Natural Egyptian, clear, calm, professional. Use إحنا and خلّينا نشوف and ببساطة where they help. No heavy Modern Standard Arabic. No exaggerated slang. Numbers are spoken naturally in Egyptian but displayed as Western digits.
glossary.register_en: Plain, direct, unhurried. Short sentences. No hype, no "imagine that…", no rhetorical questions that are not real prediction prompts. Say the number, then pause for half a beat before the next sentence — the pause is where the viewer reads the screen.
glossary.never_translate_rule: Explain them in Egyptian Arabic the first time they appear, then use the original term naturally.
glossary.on_screen: Western digits, Latin terms in LTR isolates, Egyptian Arabic copy (no MSA), no per-letter animation (04 section 3.4).

concepts.def_en: Fast, temporary working memory holding data and running programs; its contents vanish when the process ends or power is lost.
concepts.def_ar: الذاكرة السريعة المؤقتة اللي بتشيل الداتا والبرامج الشغالة؛ اللي فيها بيضيع لما الـprocess يقفل أو الكهربا تقطع.
concepts.failure: Assuming data in RAM survives a crash or restart, so unsaved work is lost.

concepts.def_en: Persistent storage, far slower than RAM, that keeps data after power-off; when full, everything else starts failing strangely.
concepts.def_ar: تخزين دائم أبطأ بكتير من الـRAM بيحتفظ بالداتا بعد ما الجهاز يفصل؛ ولما يمتلي كل حاجة تانية بتبدأ تفشل بشكل غريب.
concepts.failure: Ignoring disk usage until it fills and unrelated services begin failing with strange errors.

concepts.def_en: An organized store of data managed by software that lets many users and programs safely r…
concepts.failure: Treating a database as a bigger spreadsheet, ignoring keys, constraints and concurrent wr…

concepts.def_en: A separate sorted lookup structure on one or more columns that lets a database find rows…
concepts.failure: Adding an index on every column; each one slows writes and may never be used.

concepts.def_en: Apache Spark: a distributed engine that processes large datasets in parallel across a clu…
concepts.failure: Using Spark for small data, where cluster overhead outweighs any speed gain.

concepts.def_en: The basic unit of storage: eight bits, able to hold 256 different values.
concepts.def_ar: أصغر وحدة تخزين عملية: تمانية bits، وبتشيل 256 قيمة مختلفة.
concepts.failure: Mixing up bits and bytes, so size estimates are off by eight times.

concepts.def_en: The agreed mapping between bytes and characters, so the same bytes display as the right text when read back.
concepts.def_ar: الاتفاق على أنهي bytes تمثّل أنهي حرف، عشان النص يتقري صح بعد ما يتخزّن.
concepts.failure: Reading a file with the wrong encoding, producing garbled Arabic characters.

components.does: One whole word (or a tatweel-joined compound like الـKafka) on screen; never split per letter.
Up to 6 kinetic words on at most 2 lines, each word arriving on its own spoken word anchor.
A technical term chip (Latin in an LTR isolate) with an optional Arabic gloss; 28 px floor if spoken.
A counter that rolls from the previous value to the target over the spoken number (preset count).
An arrow from a label to a target layer (or a named part of it, 'layer.part').
Failure beat: glitch + low thud; flashes stay <= 3/s (WCAG 2.3.1).
Fix beat: the target settles into place with a settle chime.
The shot camera: move + ease + intensity; drift always on; optional impact nudges (<= 4 px) on anchors.
Match cut between a layer of this shot and one of the next.
Lower-third caption for a source, term, speaker or location.
Draw an SVG path (stroke reveal; RTL by default for Arabic layouts).
Items on a conveyor passing stations.
A ladder of latencies (cache -> RAM -> disk -> network).
The model core: idle, thinking, streaming or error.
Trunk chapter title card (riser + sting in the SFX map).
